overview: This file documents the Japanese administration’s phased removal of small Chinese silver coins (hsiaoyang-chien) from circulation in the Kwantung Leased Territory and their replacement with Bank of Chosen notes and legally recognized coins. It contains an American consular report announcing the policy, State Department memoranda explaining its connection to currency and foreign-exchange control, a subsequent despatch transmitting the implementing legislation, and translations of three Japanese ordinances prohibiting circulation after April 1, 1936, arranging government purchases of the withdrawn coins, and immediately banning further imports. Together, the documents show how a colonial monetary policy moved from press announcement to detailed legal and administrative enforcement.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: American Chargé d’Affaires ad interim in Tokyo

subfiles.title: Despatch announcing prohibition of small Chinese silver coinage
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, American Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the announced plan to prohibit small Chinese silver coins in the Kwantung Leased Territory beginning in April 1936.
subfiles.summary: Grummon reports a December announcement that Kwantung would gradually prohibit small Chinese silver coins, replacing them with Bank of Chosen notes and arranging purchase of existing coins at a reasonable price.

subfiles.title: State Department memorandum on ordinances for taking up silver coinage
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Explains that an attached Dairen despatch transmits ordinances implementing the withdrawal of silver coinage from the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: Memo identifies a December 1935 Dairen despatch transmitting ordinances on withdrawing mostly-Chinese silver coinage, linked to earlier December despatches.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting ordinances prohibiting small silver coinage
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits three ordinances governing the prohibition, redemption, and importation of small silver coins in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: Consul forwards Imperial Ordinance 313 and Kwantung Ordinances 73-74, prohibiting small-coin circulation after April 1, 1936, setting an April-June purchase window, and immediately banning further imports.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 313 on hsiaoyang-chien
subfiles.about: Prohibits hsiaoyang-chien after April 1, 1936, and establishes their purchase and replacement by Bank of Chosen currency.
subfiles.summary: Ordinance 313 bans hsiaoyang-chien circulation after April 1936, requiring government purchase, letting pre-March-31 obligations settle in silver but later ones only in Bank of Chosen currency.

subfiles.title: Kwantung Bureau Ordinance No. 73 on purchasing hsiaoyang-chien
subfiles.from: Jiro Minami, Ambassador Extraordinary of Japan
subfiles.about: Sets the institutions and period for government-authorized purchases of withdrawn hsiaoyang-chien.
subfiles.summary: Ordinance 73 has designated banks purchase small silver coins under Ordinance 313, with commissions and prices announced separately, running April 1 through June 30, 1936.

subfiles.title: Kwantung Bureau Ordinance No. 74 prohibiting imports of hsiaoyang-chien
subfiles.about: Immediately prohibits importing or preparing to import small silver coins into the Kwantung territory and prescribes criminal penalties.
subfiles.summary: Ordinance 74 bans importing or preparing to import small silver coins, penalizing violators with up to a year's hard labor or a fine, extending liability to employers.

subfiles.title: State Department memorandum on currency control in Kwantung
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Summarizes the currency-control purpose of the December 10 and 16 Dairen despatches.
subfiles.summary: Memo says Kwantung aimed to withdraw mostly-Chinese circulating silver coinage to tighten currency and exchange control, introducing paper money gradually.

interest: Shows Kwantung's 1935-36 withdrawal of small Chinese silver coinage, with timetables, penalties, and exchange-control context.
